newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - February 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - February 25.

text.p: The following were the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Defence Ministry orders police to step up security for President Kumaratunga's estranged brother Anura Bandaranaike, after he complained his life was threatened. Bandaranaike is a member of the main opposition United National Party (UNP).

Viraj Ratnatilleke, a suspect in this month's killing of ruling coalition lawmaker Nalanda Ellawala, surrenders to a magistrate after absconding for more than two weeks. He is the son of former UNP mayor Mahinda Ratnatilleke, a key suspect, who is already in police custody.
Speaker K.B. Ratnayake calls for meeting of main political parties to end confrontational politics ahead of next month's local government elections.
Government medical officers to stage a walkout on Thursday in protest of non-revision of salary.
Government says those possessing unlicenced firearms can be punished with death penalty.
Government asks public to report anyone who possesses unlicenced firearms.
Troops capture an area of 2,000 square km along the northern Mannar-Vavuniya highway in the latest offensive concluded last week, army official says.
Troops consolidate along the Mannar-Vavuniya highway captured from Tamil rebels in the army's latest offensive.
